:::{#def-consistent}
#### Consistent estimator

Let $\hparam_n$ be an estimator of $\param$ computed from $n$ observations.
The estimator is **consistent** if, for every distance $\varepsilon > 0$,
the probability that it lands at least $\varepsilon$ away from $\param$
goes to zero as the sample size grows [@wikipedia_consistent_estimator]:

$$
\lim_{n \to \infty} \Prf{\abs{\hparam_n - \param} \ge \varepsilon} = 0
$$ {#eq-consistent}

In words, $\hparam_n$
[converges in probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/limit-theorems.html#def-convergence-in-probability)
to $\param$, which we write $\hparam_n \inprob \param$.

Source: @CaseBerg01 [Def.\ 10.1.1];
@wikipedia_consistent_estimator.
:::
